questions.solution:
Option (1): ÷ and X

After swapping ÷ and X , the equation becomes:

20 X 5 + 6 ÷ 2 - 4

Now solve:

20 X 5 + 6 ÷ 2 - 4

=> 100 + 3 - 4 = 99 ≠ 18

Option (1) is incorrect.

Option (2): + and -

After swapping + and - , the equation becomes:

20 ÷ 5 - 6 X 2 + 4

=> 4 - 12 + 4 = -4 ≠ 18

Option (2) is incorrect.

Option (3): ÷ and -

After swapping ÷ and - , the equation becomes:

20 - 5 + 6 X 2 ÷ 4

=> 20 - 5 + 3 = 18

Equation is correct.

Option (4): + and ÷

After swapping + and ÷, the equation becomes:

20 + 5 ÷ 6 X 2 - 4

Now solve:

5 ÷ 6 X 2 = 10⁄6

=> 20 + 10⁄6 - 4 ≠ 18

Option (4) is incorrect.

questions.question: If 3cotA = 4, then find the value of (3sinA - 4cosA). यदि 3cotA = 4 है, तो (3sinA - 4cosA) का मान ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.solution:
Given: 3 cot A = 4

So, cot A = 4/3

This forms a 3 - 4 - 5 right triangle.

Therefore,

sin A = 3/5

cos A = 4/5

Now evaluate the expression:

3 sin A − 4 cos A

= 3 X (3/5) − 4 X (4/5)

= 9/5 − 16/5

= −7/5

Therefore, the value of 3 sin A − 4 cos A is −7/5.

questions.question: Change the following from active to passive: They don't allow smoking here.
questions.questionHtml:
Change the following from active to passive:

They don't allow smoking here.
questions.solution:
Tense

Present simple active → Present simple passive

Structure

Active: Subject + do not + base verb + object

Passive: Object + is not + past participle

Why the correct option is right

Option (2) correctly:

· Moves smoking to the subject position,

· Converts don't allow to isn't allowed,

· Retains present-time general rule.

Why the other options are incorrect

1) Present perfect changes the time reference.

3) Past tense is incorrect.

4) Introduces obligation, changing meaning.

Correct Passive:

Smoking isn't allowed here.

questions.question: A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech. John said, "I shall return soon."
questions.questionHtml:
A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech.

John said, "I shall return soon."

options.text: John said he will return soon.
options.html: John said he will return soon.

options.text: John said he would return soon.
options.html: John said he would return soon.

options.text: John said he shall return soon.
options.html: John said he shall return soon.

questions.solution:
Structure

Direct: Subject + shall + base verb

Indirect: Subject + said + subject + would + base verb

Why the correct option is right

Option (2) correctly:

· Changes first-person pronoun (I → he),

· Applies tense backshift (shall → would) due to past reporting verb said,

· Maintains meaning and time reference.

Why the other options are incorrect

1) will violates tense backshift rule.

3) Retains shall, which is incorrect after a past reporting verb.

4) Uses present tense, changing meaning.

Correct Indirect:

John said he would return soon.

questions.question: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: Had the analysts been given (1)/ access to the longitudinal data sooner, (2)/ they could have refined their projections (3)/ with greater accurateness. (4)/
questions.questionHtml:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

Had the analysts been given (1)/ access to the longitudinal data sooner, (2)/ they could have refined their projections (3)/ with greater accurateness. (4)/
questions.solution:
The error lies in "with greater accurateness."

Accurate → accuracy (noun).

Accurateness is either non-standard or stylistically incorrect in formal English. The correct noun is accuracy.

Why the other parts are correct

1) Correct use of conditional inversion (Had + subject + past participle).

2) Correct infinitive phrase and preposition.

3) Correct modal perfect construction (could have refined).

Corrected sentence:

Had the analysts been given access to the longitudinal data sooner, they could have refined their projections with greater accuracy.

questions.question: A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech. The botanist sighed that the rare orchid had germinated, only to succumb to a latent fungal blight.
questions.questionHtml:
A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech.

The botanist sighed that the rare orchid had germinated, only to succumb to a latent fungal blight.

options.text: The botanist sighed, "The rare orchid did germinate, only to succumb to a latent fungal blight."
options.html: The botanist sighed, "The rare orchid did germinate, only to succumb to a latent fungal blight."

options.text: The botanist sighed, "A rare orchid had germinated only to succumb to a latent fungal blight."

options.text: The botanist sighed, "Rare orchid germinates but succumbs to fungus."
options.html: The botanist sighed, "Rare orchid germinates but succumbs to fungus."

questions.solution:
Tense

Past perfect (indirect speech) → Simple past (direct speech)

Structure

Indirect: Reporting verb + that + past perfect clause

Direct: Reporting verb + " " + simple past clause

Why the correct option is right

Option (3) correctly:

· Removes the conjunction that,

· Shifts past perfect (had germinated) to simple past (germinated), which is standard when restoring direct narration,

· Preserves the sequence of events and the original meaning without adding emphasis.

Why the other options are incorrect

1) did germinate adds unnecessary emphatic stress not present in the original.

2) Retains had germinated, which is unnecessary and stylistically incorrect in direct speech here.

4) Grammatically incomplete and meaning is distorted.

Correct Direct:

The botanist sighed, "The rare orchid germinated, only to succumb to a latent fungal blight."

questions.question: Identify the grammatical function of the phrase "offering a direct conduit between creator and audience" in the sentence: "The platform enables unparalleled autonomy, offering a direct conduit between creator and audience, unmediated by corporate gatekeepers."
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the grammatical function of the phrase "offering a direct conduit between creator and audience" in the sentence:

"The platform enables unparalleled autonomy, offering a direct conduit between creator and audience, unmediated by corporate gatekeepers."

options.text: Present participial phrase functioning as an adverb
options.html: Present participial phrase functioning as an adverb

options.text: Noun phrase acting as an object
options.html: Noun phrase acting as an object

questions.solution:
The phrase "offering a direct conduit between creator and audience" explains how the platform enables autonomy. It adds supplementary information about the manner and result of enabling autonomy, not a defining characteristic of a noun.

Support from the passage

The structure "enables unparalleled autonomy, offering .." shows a present participial phrase that modifies the main clause, describing an accompanying action or effect.

Why the other options are incorrect

1) An adjective phrase would directly modify a noun, which is not the case here.

3) It does not function as a noun or object of a verb.

4) An absolute phrase has its own subject, which this phrase lacks.

questions.question: In the sentence "Far beyond the superficial glitz of viral videos, contemporary content creators must navigate a labyrinthine ecosystem encompassing algorithmic unpredictability..." questions.questionHtml:
In the sentence "Far beyond the superficial glitz of viral videos, contemporary content creators must navigate a labyrinthine ecosystem encompassing algorithmic unpredictability..."

options.text: Prepositional phrase functioning as a noun
options.html: Prepositional phrase functioning as a noun

questions.solution:

Support from the passage

The phrase precedes the main clause and establishes a contextual limitation, signaling that creators deal with complexities beyond appearances.

Why the other options are incorrect

1) It does not rename a noun, so it is not an appositive.

3) It does not act as a noun within the sentence.

4) It lacks an implied subject - verb relationship required for an absolute phrase.

questions.question: Rearrange the following sentences in correct order to make a logical passage: 1) The project team reviewed the proposal. 2) Adjustments were made to improve its feasibility. 3) A budget was created based on the revised proposal. 4) The proposal was then submitted for approval.
questions.questionHtml:
Rearrange the following sentences in correct order to make a logical passage:

1) The project team reviewed the proposal.

2) Adjustments were made to improve its feasibility.

3) A budget was created based on the revised proposal.

4) The proposal was then submitted for approval.
questions.solution:
The sequence follows a clear review → refinement → submission → budgeting workflow.

Sentence 1 appropriately opens the passage by stating the initial action - the project team reviews the proposal.

Sentence 2 logically follows because adjustments are typically made after a review to improve feasibility.

Sentence 4 comes next, as the revised proposal is then submitted for approval.

Sentence 3 concludes the sequence, since a budget is created based on the revised (and approved) proposal.

Why the other options are incorrect

2) 3-2-4-1 - begins with budgeting before review and revision, which is illogical.

3) 4-3-2-1 - starts with submission before review and adjustments.

4) 2-4-1-3 - places adjustments before the initial review.

Final correct sequence:

1 → 2 → 4 → 3

questions.question: Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful passage: 1) The blueprint is finalized after approval from stakeholders. 2. First, a basic framework is proposed. 3. Then revisions are made after discussions. 4. Finally, execution begins as per plan.
questions.questionHtml:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful passage:

1) The blueprint is finalized after approval from stakeholders. 2. First, a basic framework is proposed. 3. Then revisions are made after discussions. 4. Finally, execution begins as per plan.
questions.solution:
The passage follows a clear process-based chronological sequence, reinforced by explicit connectors (First, Then, Finally).

Sentence 2 is the correct opening sentence because it introduces the initial step using the marker "First", which must begin the sequence.

Sentence 3 logically follows, as revisions are made after discussions, signaled by "Then."

Sentence 1 comes next, showing that the blueprint is finalized once approvals are obtained.

Sentence 4 concludes the passage with "Finally," indicating the execution stage.

Why the other options are incorrect

1) 2-1-3-4 - places finalization before revisions, breaking logical flow.

2) 1-3-2-4 - begins with approval without introducing the framework.

4) 3-2-1-4 - starts with revisions before proposal.

Final correct sequence:

2 → 3 → 1 → 4

questions.question: Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure: The candidates were found to have been submitting forged documents during verification.

Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure:

The candidates were found to have been submitting forged documents during verification.

Structure
